source.title: The Termination Circuit (how reasoning models stop thinking).

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full post, not the linked paper. It contains apparent omissions in a few phrases (for example, a definition and some locations in the reasoning are missing).
record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on when reasoning models emit </think>, not on refusal or the refusal direction in the claim. Its single-direction steering results concern stopping, a different behavior.
record.gate_note: The post reports results about answer sufficiency and termination, including steering, MLP ablation, and state patching. These are recorded as findings about a related but different behavior, not as tests of the refusal versions. No values used only to choose a layer or component are recorded as separate rows.
record.test_reason: The post studies when Qwen3 reasoning models emit </think>, using answer splicing, MLP ablation, state patching and residual-stream steering. It never measures refusal, harmful versus harmless instructions, or a refusal direction. Its finding that no single direction controls termination concerns a different behaviour. So it does not test any version, including V8. It also never mentions refusal, so 'discusses' is the loosest fit among the available relations.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author concludes that stopping is a high-dimensional late-MLP verification gate that checks a stated answer against the model's internal answer. It is not a sufficiency detector or a single steerable direction. The author recommends eliciting candidate answers earlier to reduce overthinking.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies reasoning-chain sufficiency and termination-token behavior using answer splicing, circuit interventions, and steering. It does not study refusal directions or refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported steering effect depends on how close the gate is to firing: steering from a normal mid-chain boundary recovers only about 20% of the full-state patching effect, while steering near firing can tip the gate to some degree.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen3-1.7B, splicing the model's own correct answer after the sufficiency point makes </think> the greedy next token in 94% of traces. Mismatched or mistimed answers do so in 0-19%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-model termination is gated by a stated answer matching the internally computed answer.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the top 4 termination MLPs prevents stopping, while reasoning stays coherent and perplexity barely changes. Patching the trigger state transfers the stop decision in ~99% of cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A localized late-MLP circuit causally controls reasoning termination.

fits_no_version.finding: The best single residual-stream direction recovers only ~20% of the full-state patching effect from a mid-chain boundary. Steering works partially only when the gate is near firing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Termination in reasoning models is not mediated by a single steerable direction (an analogue of single-direction claims for a different behaviour).

fits_no_version.finding: The post reports that the same late-MLP gate replicates in Qwen3-8B and Magistral-Small-24B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The termination gate generalizes across reasoning-model scales.

record.problems: The supplied post gives few methodological details and no uncertainty estimates. Several results are reported only as approximate percentages or qualitative statements, and the linked paper is not included in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The post also reports that one MLP contributes ~40% of the </think> logit, the top 8 components account for 71%, attention heads contribute very little, and the stop margin jumps when the final-answer sentence is written. These termination-logit attribution and trajectory details do not test any refusal version and were left out of the rows.

untested.parts: No refusal direction is extracted, ablated or added, and no capability check is made after a refusal intervention.
No jailbreaks and no adversarial training against ablation.
No multi-direction or cone analysis of refusal. The high-dimensionality claim is about termination.
No harmfulness or refusal representations are measured.
No transfer of a refusal direction. The 8B and 24B replications concern the termination gate.
Reasoning models are studied, but only for termination, not refusal.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to 'none'. The post is internally inconsistent about when the answer is settled: the summary says 'about halfway', while the body says a median of ~30% of the CoT. r1 uses the 30% figure. The linked PDF was not supplied. There are no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Refusal-direction discovery, refusal removal or induction, and preservation of other abilities after refusal-direction intervention.
No weight-edit ablation of refusal is reported.
No jailbreak or training-against-ablation robustness experiment is reported.
No refusal representation is tested as an affine structure, cone, or multiple directions.
No harmfulness judgment or refusal decision is measured.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or training stages is tested.
No refusal training procedure or its effect on directionality is tested.
The post studies reasoning-model termination, not whether the refusal-direction claim holds in reasoning models.
